newsitem.title: FRANCE: Trash makes up 35 percent of goods on French roads.
newsitem.headline: Trash makes up 35 percent of goods on French roads.

text.p: Rubbish makes up about a third of all goods transported within France, and almost all of that trash is carried by truck, French researchers said on Tuesday.

Researchers at the French environmental and energy agency ADEME said a new study of the growing problem of rubbish transport in France recommends that more trash be shipped by rail or water in order to save energy and cut pollution.
The study is due to be released in September.
"About 35 percent of the tonnage of goods transported in France is comprised of rubbish, and more than 95 percent of that is transported by truck," said ADEME's Christophe Ripert.
"That is as if one out of every three trucks on the road in France was loaded with rubbish," he said in a telephone interview from ADEME offices in the Riviera city Cannes.
"We must try to put systems in place to find other means of transport, such as by water or rail, which pollute less and use less energy," he said.
The ADEME study found that just 2.4 percent of rubbish is shipped by rail in France and less than one percent by water.
More than 800 million tonnes of rubbish is generated in France, whether by industry, agriculture or households, according to the study.
About half of that is transported somewhere, whether for recycling, processing or disposal.
The average distance by which rubbish is transported is about 43 km (26 miles), Ripert said.

The amount of trash that must be transported within France is growing rapidly because more consumer goods are packaged and also because more rubbish is being recycled or otherwise processed, Ripert said.
